2.text: adopt the dress and the mode of life of the Chukchee, which are very dif-

3.text: ferent from Tungus life. Only a few of these Tungus women hold to their

4.text: former customs, and then the life of the family presents a double character.

5.text: In the winter-time they live in a Chukchee “genuine house,” drive reindeer in

6.text: Chukchee harness, etc. In summer they live in a Tungus tent, ride Tungus

7.text: reindeer, hunt wild reindeer and mountain-sheep. With a Tungus wife comes

8.text: her family, hungry and careless, often the whole clan; and they expect to

9.text: receive help from their new kinsman. So even a very rich Chukchee, after

10.text: a few years of Tungus marriage, usually becomes poorer, and then quite poor.

11.text: To refuse a Tungus kinsfolk a reindeer for slaughter is almost impossible,

12.text: because the people of that tribe often stay on the verge of starvation, and

13.text: the Chukchee brother-in-law has to relieve them, even almost against his will.

14.text: In the second category of such mixed marriages are the Tungus men

15.text: who marry Chukchee women. A young Tungus man who is tired of the

16.text: hungry life of a polar hunter may come to a Chukchee camp and be admit-

17.text: ted, at first as an assistant herdsman, then as an adopted son-in-law. A

18.text: well-to-do Chukchee family, when short of male workers, will not ask about

19.text: the tribe of the new-comer, but desires only watchfulness and activity in taking

20.text: care of the herd. I know a Tungus family on the Dry Anui River that

21.text: consists of five full-grown brothers. All of them married into a Chukchee

22.text: family; and now each has a large herd, received with the wife. Of course,

23.text: such Tungus adopted by the Chukchee lead the usual Chukchee life, and

24.text: their children rarely speak their father’s language. Among all tribes the house-

25.text: hold life is regulated mostly by a woman; and a Chukchee woman is quite

26.text: unable to abandon her national dress and her mode of living, and adopt those

27.text: of alien origin. Therefore I know of hardly a single case where a Chukchee

28.text: woman has married into a Tungus family in order to live the Tungus life.

29.text: What has been said concerning the Tungus may also be said of Chukchee

30.text: marriages with the Yukaghir of the West Kolyma tundra, who are still poorer

31.text: than the Tungus, and who are only too glad to be adopted into a Chukchee

33.text: As to marriages between the Chukchee and Russian creoles or Rus-

34.text: sianized natives, I know of about twenty cases, half of which belong to the

35.text: past, and half to the present.

36.text: I visited, one after another, all the mixed Chukchee-Russian couples in

37.text: various parts of the Chukchee territory; and in almost all cases I found that

38.text: Russian or Russianized women were married to Chukchee men. All these

39.text: women belonged to very poor families, and marriage with a reindeer-breeder

40.text: was the only means of warding off severe hunger, at least for the time being.

41.text: Some of these women were paid for with twenty or thirty slaughtered rein-

42.text: deer, others with only two or three. Usually the families to which they had
